Read the relevant section before that class of change. - `docs/test-lanes.md` owns named test lanes. Prefer the `pnpm run test:*` aliases over copying raw Vitest selectors. - `repository/topology.json` owns workspace boundaries and release bundles. - `package.json` owns the current command names. Inspect it instead of copying command details into new documentation. - Use the GitHub MCP server for GitHub operations. Use `gh` only when the GitHub MCP server cannot complete the operation because of a token problem. ## Runtime and package manager Use mise for Node.js and pnpm. The repository pins Node.js 24 and pnpm 12 in `mise.toml`; install the pinned tools before running development commands: ```bash mise install ``` Run Node.js and pnpm commands through mise so they do not fall back to system installations. Use `mise exec -- pnpm ...`, `mise exec -- npx ...`, and `mise exec -- node ...` in setup, validation, and troubleshooting commands. Git hooks are managed by hk. After `mise install`, enable them once per clone with: ```bash mise exec hk -- hk install --mise ``` ## Repository shape and boundaries The root is a private workspace orchestrator and has no runtime `src/` tree. The six workspaces are: - `packages/hevy-client` — runtime-neutral native-fetch Hevy client, curated exports, and Kubb-generated API types/schemas. - `packages/operations` — runtime-neutral reusable Hevy domain operations. - `packages/core` — runtime-neutral MCP server construction, tools, prompts, resources, execution, and safe diagnostics. - `packages/node` — public Node package `hevy-mcp`; Node lifecycle, stdio and local Streamable HTTP transports, telemetry, and Node built-ins. - `packages/worker` — private Cloudflare Worker Streamable HTTP and optional OAuth adapter. - `packages/cli` — public Node package `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`; the standalone Hevy command-line client. The dependency direction is `hevy-client -> operations -> core`, with `core` also depending directly on `hevy-client`; Node, Worker, and CLI are adapters that consume the runtime-neutral packages. Adapters do not import one another. Keep Node built-ins and Cloudflare bindings out of `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core`. Keep Node-only lifecycle, transport, telemetry, and observability in `packages/node`; keep Worker bindings and OAuth in `packages/worker`. ## Generated client Treat every file under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` as generated output. Change the OpenAPI source or the Kubb configuration, then regenerate: ```bash mise exec -- pnpm run openapi # refreshes the upstream spec; needs network access mise exec -- pnpm run build:client mise exec -- pnpm run check:openapi mise exec -- pnpm run check:generated ``` Review the complete generated diff. Consumers use the curated `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types`, and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas` exports; generated API functions and `.kubb` internals are private. Upstream schema corrections belong in `scripts/openapi-spec.js` so regeneration remains reproducible. ## MCP and type-safety conventions MCP tools live in `packages/core/src/tools/`. Follow the existing tool-definition pattern when adding or changing one: 1. Put the Zod input shape in the relevant tool file or `tools/input-schemas.ts`. 2. Derive handler arguments with `InferToolParams`; keep the schema as the single source of truth for validation and types. 3. Define the response contract and output schema for read tools in `utils/response-contracts.ts`. 4. Register the definition through `tools/register.ts`, use the existing `ToolRuntime` error/observation path, and add a co-located test. 5. Measure token cost when tool descriptions or schemas materially change: `pnpm run measure:tokens`. Handlers receive inferred arguments. Keep manual argument casts, `any`, and `unknown` out of tool-handler code. Reuse the existing error policy, `withErrorHandling` path, response contracts, and safe diagnostics rather than creating parallel response or error formats. ## Secrets and runtime behavior Use `HEVY_API_KEY` through `.env` or the process environment. Keep `.env` and real keys untracked, and keep keys out of command-line arguments, URLs, logs, fixtures, screenshots, and error messages. Deterministic unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, package, and performance lanes use fake credentials and do not need a live key. Live Hevy lanes require a valid `HEVY_API_KEY`. The Node executable defaults to stdio and also supports local Streamable HTTP with `--transport http`; inspect `packages/node/README.md` or `--help` before changing transport behavior. The Worker serves stateless Streamable HTTP at `POST /mcp`, authenticates the request bearer value, and keeps OAuth optional behind the `OAUTH_KV` binding. Read the Worker section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` before changing deployment, origin, authentication, or OAuth behavior. ## Changesets and release identity Before every commit, classify the diff and run: ```bash pnpm run check:changeset ``` A change under `packages/*`, a runtime-visible behavior change, a workspace dependency change, or `cloudflare.config.ts` requires a non-empty bump Changeset. Name the changed package and every transitive shipped consumer from `repository/topology.json`; do not couple unrelated packages. The current cascade is: - `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` -> `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/operations` -> `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/core` -> `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - Node-only, Worker-only, and CLI-only changes bump only their respective package; `cloudflare.config.ts` is a Worker change. Core, client, operations, and Worker are private but versioned for internal release/deployment identity. Node and CLI are public. Merge the automated `changeset-release/main` Version Packages pull request on the routine cadence (weekly by default); reserve off-cycle releases for security fixes and high-impact user-facing bugs. An entirely no-release, repository-only change may use an eligible empty Changeset via `npx changeset --empty`; docs, CI, repository-only tests/tooling, and chores qualify only when no release trigger is present. An empty Changeset never accompanies a release trigger. Stage the Changeset before committing. ## Validation workflow For source changes, run the narrow relevant lane and the unit suite. Before a pull request, use the repository baseline from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: ```bash mise exec -- pnpm run check mise exec -- pnpm run check:types mise exec -- pnpm run build mise exec -- pnpm run test:pr mise exec -- pnpm run test:performance mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset ``` Useful focused checks include: - `pnpm run test:stdio` after MCP SDK, stdio, lifecycle, or Node transport changes. `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` uses private MCP SDK fields, so inspect compatibility after every SDK upgrade. - `pnpm run test:worker`, `pnpm run test:worker-http`, and `pnpm run worker:dry-run` after Worker changes. - `pnpm run test:pack` or `pnpm run test:pack:cli` after package entry point, binary, manifest, or published-file changes. - `pnpm run check:server-manifest` after server metadata changes. - `pnpm run check:boundaries` after workspace dependency or runtime-boundary changes. `pnpm run test:unit` is the deterministic default for local source work. `npm test` builds first and runs broad Vitest discovery; it is not a substitute for the named PR lanes. Integration, live, nightly, and live Worker commands are credential-gated and should be run only when the relevant safe credentials and environment are available. Known environment-dependent operations: - `pnpm run openapi` needs network access to the upstream Hevy API and may fail with `ENOTFOUND api.hevyapp.com` in a sandbox. - `pnpm run inspect` may time out without a correctly configured MCP client or browser environment. Treat all other documented checks, including `pnpm run check:types`, as real failures to investigate. ## Completion checklist Before reporting completion, confirm that the diff is focused, tests and checks for the changed paths passed (or their limitations are explicit), generated output is synchronized, the release requirement is satisfied, and `git status --short --branch` shows only intended files on the feature branch. This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification. @.entire/graph-agent.md # Ultracite Code Standards This project uses **Ultracite**, a zero-config preset that enforces strict code quality standards through automated formatting and linting. ## Quick Reference - **Format code**: `pnpm run fix` - **Check for issues**: `pnpm run check` - **Diagnose setup**: `pnpm exec ultracite doctor` Oxlint + Oxfmt (the underlying engine) provides robust linting and formatting. Most issues are automatically fixable. --- ## Core Principles Write code that is **accessible, performant, type-safe, and maintainable**. Focus on clarity and explicit intent over brevity. ### Type Safety & Explicitness - Use explicit types for function parameters and return values when they enhance clarity - Prefer `unknown` over `any` when the type is genuinely unknown - Use const assertions (`as const`) for immutable values and literal types - Leverage TypeScript's type narrowing instead of type assertions - Use meaningful variable names instead of magic numbers - extract constants with descriptive names ### Modern JavaScript/TypeScript - Use arrow functions for callbacks and short functions - Prefer `for...of` loops over `.forEach()` and indexed `for` loops - Use optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) for safer property access - Prefer template literals over string concatenation - Use destructuring for object and array assignments - Use `const` by default, `let` only when reassignment is needed, never `var` ### Async & Promises - Always `await` promises in async functions - don't forget to use the return value - Use `async/await` syntax instead of promise chains for better readability - Handle errors appropriately in async code with try-catch blocks - Don't use async functions as Promise executors ### React & JSX - Use function components over class components - Call hooks at the top level only, never conditionally - Specify all dependencies in hook dependency arrays correctly - Use the `key` prop for elements in iterables (prefer unique IDs over array indices) - Nest children between opening and closing tags instead of passing as props - Don't define components inside other components - Use semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for accessibility: - Provide meaningful alt text for images - Use proper heading hierarchy - Add labels for form inputs - Include keyboard event handlers alongside mouse events - Use semantic elements (`

# Validation Contract: Deepen Effect Adoption (stacked on PR #1120)

Black-box behavioral assertions that define "done" for this mission. Validators test against these specifications, not against implementation structure. Do not assert "uses Effect.retry" or "uses ManagedRuntime"; assert observable retry, cancellation, error, lifecycle, and compatibility behavior.

**Repo:** `/home/ubuntu/hevy-mcp-effect-deepening`  
**Commands:** prefix every `mise exec` with `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false`.  
**Secrets:** never print, log, or persist `HEVY_API_KEY` values, `Authorization` / `api-key` headers, or bearer tokens. Deterministic assertions use fake credentials.

**Surfaces**

| Surface | Tool | When |
|---|---|---|
| Hevy client unit | vitest (`packages/hevy-client`) | Track 1 |
| Worker validation-cache | vitest (`packages/worker`, `pnpm run test:worker`) | Track 1 |
| Core / in-process MCP | vitest + mocked MCP (`test:mcp`, `test:contract`) | Track 2 |
| Node embedding / stdio / HTTP | vitest, spawned `node`, curl (`test:stdio`, `test:pack`) | Track 3 |
| CLI | vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`) | Track 3/4 |
| Live Hevy | `pnpm run test:live`, `pnpm run test:integration` | Milestone 4 only |
| Docs | Read | Milestone 4 |
| Repo gates | `check`, `check:types`, `build`, `test:pr`, `test:performance`, `check:changeset`, `check:boundaries` | Every milestone + CROSS |

---

# Area: Client Runtime

## Surface

Who consumes this: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` callers (`createHevyClient` Promise API used by Node, CLI, Worker, and tests); `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` Effect request facade used by `@hevy-mcp/operations`; Worker bearer/OAuth validation via `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` in `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`. End users never call this package directly; MCP tools and the CLI collapse through these Promise/Effect boundaries.

How it is tested: vitest in `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/worker`; TestClock and fake timers for delays; mocked `fetch` (no live Hevy in this area).

Focused suites:
- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-local-retry-state.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/backoff.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`

## Interactions enumerated

- Construct `createHevyClient({ apiKey, baseUrl?, fetch?, timeoutMs?, maxGetRetries?, sleep?, onLog?, onRequestStart?, onRequestComplete?, onRetryWait? })`.
- Call any of the 22 Promise methods with optional `{ signal, deadline, timeoutMs }`.
- Receive a successful JSON body, or a rejected `HevyHttpError` with `code` / `status` / execution metadata.
- Observe retries: transient GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads and PUT/DELETE idempotent writes retry; POST/PATCH non-idempotent writes never retry.
- Observe retry budget: default `maxGetRetries = 3` (4 attempts); delays start at 300 ms, double each retry, cap at 5000 ms, plus bounded jitter.
- Observe 429 handling: client retries 429 and honors `Retry-After` as a lower bound, still jittered, clipped to remaining deadline.
- Observe per-attempt timeout and overall operation deadline.
- Observe the one extra read attempt after a client-derived attempt deadline. Caller-supplied `deadline` is never extended.
- Abort via `AbortSignal`: already-aborted, mid-fetch, while reading the body, during backoff. Concurrent requests stay isolated.
- Consume the internal Effect facade: same retry/timeout/abort counts; tagged errors.
- Operations pass `descriptor.safety` into composed Hevy calls; raw client calls fall back to HTTP-method mapping.
- Worker `validateHevyApiKeyResilient`: cache hit skips Hevy; miss validates; retries transient failures with delays `[300, 600]`; never retries 429; abort/deadline stop the loop; cache never stores the raw API key.

# Area: Core Runtime

## Surface

`packages/core` is the MCP server the adapters embed. A client talks to it over the MCP protocol (in-process mocked client in `test:mcp` / `test:contract`, or any stdio/HTTP adapter).

**Intended catalog-cancellation policy:** a cache-miss load is interruptible. If the cancelling waiter is the **only** waiter, the shared Hevy load is cancelled. If the canceller is **one of several** waiters, that waiter is interrupted and the others keep the still-needed load. `refresh: true` still bypasses a hit and loads fresh data.

## Interactions enumerated

- MCP `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` (reads and writes, unknown names, invalid args, missing client/operation, Hevy failures, abort, deadline).
- MCP `resources/list` and `resources/read` of the four `hevy://` URIs, including abort of `hevy://exercise-templates`.
- MCP `prompts/list` and `prompts/get`.
- Catalog hit / miss / TTL / refresh / failed load / dual waiter topologies.
- Server close / `lifecycleSignal` abort interrupting in-flight cache loads.
- Observer, MCP logging, and cache-callback failures never change outcomes.
- Promise `createHevyMcpServer` façade still builds a working server.

## 1. What we are changing

PR #1120 already made `@hevy-mcp/operations` Effect-first and routed MCP tools and CLI commands through those programs, collapsing Effect at Promise adapter boundaries. This mission deepens Effect so it becomes the **actual control structure**, not a delay calculator or a Promise wrapper.

Three tracks, plus a last-mile live validation:

| Track | Package(s) | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| Client runtime | `packages/hevy-client`, `packages/worker` (validation-cache only) | Retry/timeout/interruption via `Effect.retry` + `Schedule` + `Effect.timeout*` + fiber interruption |
| Core runtime | `packages/core` | Scoped server construction, interruptible tool runs, typed error channel, Logger/Metrics |
| Node adapter | `packages/node` | Lifecycle, shutdown, telemetry, Streamable HTTP as scoped Effect programs |
| Live e2e | docs + live lanes | Verify against real Hevy API; update README/architecture docs |

**Out of scope**

- Worker adapter beyond the validation-cache retry loop (OAuth, bindings, request handling stay Promise-based).
- Replacing Zod with Effect Schema for tool input/response contracts.
- Effect Config for env/CLI parsing (config.ts / arguments.ts stay throwing parsers unless a later feature needs them).
- Editing `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/`.
- Touching `/home/ubuntu/hevy-mcp` (the original checkout). Work only in the worktree.

## 3. Scope hierarchy (the central design)

### 3.1 Process scope — `packages/node`

Owned by `runNodeLifecycle`. Acquires:

- Process exception tracking (install/remove listeners).
- Telemetry providers (OTel tracer/meter, Sentry). Finalizer = `forceFlush` + shutdown.
- Graceful-shutdown listeners (SIGINT/SIGTERM). Forced-exit is `Effect.race(shutdown, Effect.sleep(5s))`, not a hand-rolled `setTimeout`.
- The MCP transport: stdio pipe, or the Streamable HTTP server (itself a Scope that owns sessions).

Public Promise façades (`createNodeMcpServer`, `runStdioServer`, `runServer`) remain. They collapse a process-scoped Effect via `Effect.runPromise`. Effect-typed variants may be added (e.g. `createNodeMcpServerEffect`) because public Effect exports are allowed.

`packages/node/src/index.ts` **must stay side-effect-free** (embedding contract). Telemetry init moves off module-import time into the Layer that the runtime program provides. The documented import-order constraint in `runtime.ts` goes away once telemetry is a Layer.

### 3.2 Server scope — `packages/core`

Owned by `createHevyMcpServer` (which becomes Effect-returning internally; the Promise wrapper stays for existing callers). Acquires:

- Exercise-template `Cache.make`. Lookup **must** read `ToolExecutionContextService` (or equivalent) so a cache-miss load is interruptible and deadline-bounded. The cache is finalized when the server Scope closes.
- A long-lived Layer context (HevyOperations, HevyClient, catalog, observer). Built with `ManagedRuntime` or an explicitly closed `Scope` — **never** `Effect.runSync(Scope.make())` that is never closed.
- The MCP `McpServer` instance.

`lifecycleSignal` from the Node adapter interrupts this scope on process shutdown.

### 3.3 Request scope — per tool / resource invocation

Created by `runtime.forExecution({ signal: context.mcpReq.signal, ... })`. Acquires:

- Merged abort signal (lifecycle ∪ request).
- Derived deadline (`nextExecution.deadline ?? serverDeadline ?? now + timeoutMs`).
- Request-local service overlay if needed.

`runToolEffect` **must** pass the request signal into `Effect.runPromise(program, { signal })` (or `runFork` + interrupt) so MCP cancellation interrupts the fiber, not only the underlying fetch.

The `exercise-templates` resource currently calls `.effect()` with no execution options. It must pass `scoped.execution` like the other resources.

## 4. Track 1 — Client runtime

### 4.1 Retry interpreter (`packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`)

**Today:** `Effect.gen` + `while (true)` + `Schedule.toStep` used as a delay iterator. `canRetryAttempt` is a separate predicate. `withTimeout` is a hand-rolled Promise.race. `createExecutionSignal` is a hand-rolled AbortController + `setTimeout`. `withExecutionSignal` (`execution.ts`) is exported and unused.

**Target:**

- One attempt is an Effect. The retry driver is `Effect.retry(schedule)` (or equivalent Effect 4 combinator). The Schedule owns:
  - Recurrence count (`Schedule.recurs(maxGetRetries)`).
  - Delay (`Schedule.addDelay` with existing `getRetryDelayMs`, including Retry-After union + jitter).
  - “Should I retry this error?” via `Schedule.whileInput` (or Effect 4 equivalent) wrapping `canRetryAttempt`.
- The “one free read retry after deadline” branch (`hevy-client-kubb.ts:877-903`) folds into schedule composition (`Schedule.recurs(1)` gated on deadline-exceeded + `safety === "read"` + no caller-supplied deadline), not a hardcoded side channel.
- Per-attempt timeout is `Effect.timeout*` around the fetch/body-parse, not `withTimeout`.
- Fiber interruption is the cancellation mechanism. AbortSignal is bridged **at the fetch edge only** (so native `fetch` still cancels). `abortOnInterruption` listeners and `createExecutionSignal` deadline timers go away or become thin adapters.
- Use `withExecutionSignal` inside `createRequestEffect`, or delete it. Do not leave two cleanup paths.

**Safety:** `operation.descriptor.safety` (from `@hevy-mcp/operations`) drives retry decisions for composed operations. HTTP-method mapping (`operationSafetyForMethod`) remains the fallback for raw client calls that have no descriptor. Non-idempotent writes are never retried.

**Behavior improvements are allowed** (user-approved). Flag every policy change in the worker handoff: retry counts, backoff curve, Retry-After handling, which errors retry, the free deadline-retry. Default to preserving current observable policy unless the improvement is a clear correctness/safety win (e.g. interruptible cache loads, no retry on non-idempotent writes at the operation layer).

**Promise boundary:** `HevyClient` stays Promise-typed for existing callers. Effect-typed request APIs may be exported. Tagged error classes at the Promise boundary stay discriminable (`ApiError`, `NetworkError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError`, `ValidationError`, plus the existing `HEVY_*` codes). Do not mutate errors in place (`applyRetryExhaustion` today mutates `error.code`); produce a new tagged error.

### 4.2 Worker validation-cache (`packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`)

**Today:** imperative `for` loop, delays `[300, 600]`, `delay()` that *resolves* on abort (forcing a post-sleep re-check). Excludes 429 while the client treats 429 as transient.

**Target:** `Effect.retry` with a composed Schedule (exponential 300ms, jittered, `whileInput(isRetryableValidationFailure)`, intersected with remaining deadline). Drop the custom `delay()`. Keep the 429 exclusion if it is still the right policy for a validation probe — document why in a comment next to the Schedule predicate.

Do **not** otherwise change Worker request handling, OAuth, or bindings.

## 5. Track 2 — Core runtime

### 5.1 Server construction (`packages/core/src/server.ts`)

`createHevyMcpServer` today is synchronous and does `Effect.runSync(Cache.make({ lookup: (_key) => templateListAll.effect() }))` with no execution options and no Scope.

**Target:**

- Construction is an Effect that requires `Scope`. The Promise wrapper (`createHevyMcpServer`) runs that Effect in a scope the adapter owns, or returns `{ server, close }` / uses `ManagedRuntime`.
- Cache lookup reads per-request execution context from the environment. A cancelled MCP request must not leave a full paginated template fetch running against Hevy.

### 5.2 Tool runtime (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.ts`)

**Today:** `buildServiceContext` does `Effect.runSync(Scope.make())` + `Layer.build` and never closes the scope (comment: “outlives this call”). `runToolEffect` calls `Effect.runPromise` with no signal. **Target:**

**Today:** `instanceof` cascades plus string-sniffing (`classificationText.includes("network")`). Defensive `try/catch` returning `undefined`.

Shared cache load must be interruptible. `replaceSharedCacheLoad` / `bypassCache` / `requestGeneration` exist because the lookup currently ignores execution; after lookup reads context, simplify if those workarounds become redundant — but keep bypass-cache behavior for callers that need a fresh fetch.

Evidence: Rejection/exit before listen/connect. Message exact.

### VAL-NODE-010: Unreachable Hevy during probe does not crash startup
When the startup probe fails with a safe network diagnostic (`ENOTFOUND`, `ETIMEDOUT`, HTTP 5xx, etc.), the executable continues and still starts the transport. stderr contains `Warning: HEVY_API_KEY could not be validated during startup` plus at most a bounded diagnostic. Arbitrary error messages / secrets from the probe must not appear.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: Server construction proceeds. stderr includes the warning and allowed diagnostic; forbidden substrings are absent.

### VAL-NODE-011: Stdio initialize and tools/list work over JSON-RPC
A spawned `hevy-mcp` stdio process with a fake/valid key accepts newline-delimited JSON-RPC `initialize` and `tools/list` on stdin and writes JSON-RPC results on stdout. Shutdown/log lines go to stderr, never stdout.
Tool: node (spawned process)
Evidence: `initialize` result has `protocolVersion`. `tools/list` result has a `tools` array. stdout is parseable JSON-RPC frames only.

### VAL-NODE-012: SIGINT and SIGTERM shut down gracefully
A running stdio or HTTP server treated with SIGINT or SIGTERM logs `Shutting down gracefully after SIGINT|SIGTERM` on stderr, closes the MCP target, flushes stdout, removes the signal listeners, and exits 0 when close succeeds. Active work tied to the lifecycle abort signal is cancelled before/during close. A second signal during the same shutdown does not start a second close.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: Child-process regression: backpressured JSON-RPC frames fully appear on stdout before exit 0; shutdown banner only on stderr. Unit: `close` called once for SIGTERM then SIGINT; abort signal aborted; listeners count 0 after completion.

### VAL-NODE-013: Hung close forces process exit after 5 seconds
If `target.close()` (or an unrelated open handle) prevents the event loop from draining, a SIGINT/SIGTERM still terminates the process after 5 seconds. Observable outcome: process exits with code 1 when shutdown has not settled by the deadline. The fallback must not keep the process alive on its own after a successful close (timer is unref'd).
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: With a close that never settles, wall-clock time from signal to `exit` is about 5s (± test clock / fake timer). Exit code 1.

### VAL-NODE-014: HTTP initialize creates an isolated session
`POST /mcp` with a JSON-RPC `initialize` body on loopback without `Mcp-Session-Id` returns HTTP 200 and an `mcp-session-id` response header. Two initializes produce two different session ids. A subsequent `tools/list` / mocked `tools/call` with that header returns 200 and is routed only to that session.
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: Real `node:http` ephemeral port. Status 200. Distinct session ids.

### VAL-NODE-015: HTTP subsequent requests require a known session
Any non-initialize `/mcp` request (POST/GET/DELETE) without `Mcp-Session-Id` returns 400 with body `{"error":"Mcp-Session-Id header is required."}`. Unknown `Mcp-Session-Id` returns 404 with `{"error":"Unknown Mcp-Session-Id."}` (unknown id is rejected before body consumption). `initialize` that already includes `Mcp-Session-Id` returns 400 `Initialization must not include Mcp-Session-Id.` Non-`/mcp` paths return 404 `Not found`.
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: Status and JSON `error` string match. Unknown-session rejection does not hang waiting for a full body.

### VAL-NODE-016: HTTP DELETE closes the session and aborts in-flight work
`DELETE /mcp` with a valid `mcp-session-id` returns 200. A later POST with that id returns 404. If a tool call is in flight, the session lifecycle abort fires so the handler can stop; the session is not reused.
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: DELETE 200; follow-up 404; session abort signal aborted while the hanging tool is waiting.

### VAL-NODE-017: HTTP idle eviction frees session capacity
With `maxSessions: 1` and a short idle timeout, an established session that has no active response is evicted. After eviction (or explicit DELETE), a new `initialize` succeeds (200). While the slot is occupied, a new `initialize` is rejected.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: Second initialize is 429 while occupied; after DELETE or idle wait, initialize is 200. Idle timer does not evict while a response is still writable.

### VAL-NODE-018: HTTP admission rejects over-capacity with current status/body
When established sessions are at max, extra `initialize` returns **429** and body `{"error":"MCP session capacity reached. Retry after an existing session closes."}`. When initializing slots are occupied, extra `initialize` returns **503** and body `{"error":"MCP server is busy initializing sessions. Retry shortly."}`. Defaults remain maxSessions=100, maxInitializing=10 unless overridden; env overrides are bounded (invalid/zero fall back to defaults; huge values clamp).
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: Status + exact JSON error string. A hanging initialize occupies the initializing slot until abort/close.

### VAL-NODE-019: HTTP stalled body returns 408
A POST `/mcp` that sends headers but not a completing body is rejected after `bodyTimeoutMs` (default 30s; overridable, max 5 minutes) with HTTP **408** and body `{"error":"Request body timed out."}`. The connection does not hang until the client closes. Oversized body (>1_048_576 bytes) is 413 `Request body is too large.`; malformed JSON is 400 `Request body must be valid JSON.` without echoing the raw body.
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: Status 408, exact body, elapsed time ≈ configured timeout (fake clock or 10ms override in tests).

### VAL-NODE-020: HTTP close fans out session cleanup and leaks no listeners
`handle.close()` (SIGINT/SIGTERM on the HTTP process, or embedder `close()`) marks the server shutting down, aborts in-flight initializes, closes every session (transport + MCP server + idle timer), closes the `node:http` server including idle/open connections, and is idempotent (second `close()` returns the same completion). After close: `server.listening === false`, open SSE/GET streams end, pending initialize abort signals are aborted, and no session idle timers remain. New POSTs that race shutdown receive 503 `HTTP server is shutting down. Retry shortly.` Process signal listeners installed for this server are removed after shutdown completes.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: `close()` resolves; `listening` is false; hanging initialize's `lifecycleSignal.aborted === true`; stream `ended`; no extra `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` listeners attributable to the handle after completion.

### VAL-NODE-021: HTTP Host header and bearer protections
Loopback servers reject DNS-rebinding Host headers with 403 `Invalid Host header`. Non-loopback bind without `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` fails to start: `Non-loopback HTTP mode requires HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN…`. Wildcard (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) with the token: missing/wrong `Authorization` is 401 `Authorization required`; `Authorization: Bearer <token>` initialize is 200. Timing-safe compare: wrong-length header is 401, not 500.
Tool: vitest | curl
Evidence: Status/body as above. Token value does not appear in error bodies.

### VAL-NODE-022: HTTP session startup failures are structured and secret-free
If MCP server construction/connect throws, initialize returns 500 JSON with a bounded execution projection (`outcome` such as `terminal_failure`) and must not include the thrown private message. stderr may log a safe diagnostic, never the raw secret/detail.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: Status 500; body contains `"outcome":"terminal_failure"` (or the then-current bounded projection); body/stderr omit the private error string.

### VAL-NODE-023: HTTP key is probed once per process, not per session
Executable HTTP mode validates `HEVY_API_KEY` once at startup. Additional HTTP sessions do not perform another Hevy key-validation request.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: One probe call for a process that then initializes multiple HTTP sessions.

### VAL-NODE-024: Telemetry is not started by embedding import and does not run on `--help`/`--version`
OTel/Sentry must not initialize at import of `hevy-mcp`. `--help` and `--version` must not register tracer/meter providers, Sentry, or startup metrics. Telemetry, when enabled, starts only as part of actually running the server lifecycle. `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` (literal `0` only) disables all project telemetry: no Sentry init, no exporters, no periodic metric readers, `flush` is a no-op.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: Help/version processes make no telemetry network. Embedding import does not call `Sentry.init` / tracer register. `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` process starts MCP anyway.

### VAL-NODE-025: Telemetry flush on shutdown; flush failure never fails the server
Successful SIGINT/SIGTERM completion flushes telemetry with a bounded timeout (observable as shutdown still finishing even if flush hangs). CLI fatal path still attempts flush, then `process.exit(1)`. If flush throws or times out, the original exit/outcome is preserved. Tool/HTTP/admission behavior is unchanged when metric/Sentry calls throw.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: Flush invoked on graceful complete. Forced throw from flush does not reject MCP tool results, does not change HTTP 429/503/408, and does not convert a successful close into a crash before exit.

### VAL-NODE-026: Pack/install tarball exposes bin and side-effect-free index
`pnpm run test:pack` must keep: `bin.hevy-mcp = dist/cli.mjs`; `exports["."]` pointing at `dist/index.mjs` / `dist/index.d.mts`; required files `README.md`, `dist/cli.mjs`, `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/index.d.mts`, `server.json`. After `npm install <tarball>`: `hevy-mcp --help` and `--version` succeed; `import('hevy-mcp')` yields functions `createNodeMcpServer` and `runStdioServer`; spawned bin with a fake key completes MCP `initialize` + `tools/list`. Packed JS must not import `@hevy-mcp/core` or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` by those names (bundled). Public `package.json` must not declare those private workspace deps.
Tool: node (spawned process)
Evidence: Pack smoke script remaining green after the adapter change, including Effect as a bundled or declared runtime dep without breaking the private-workspace import ban.

### VAL-NODE-027: Secrets never appear in logs, HTTP bodies, or telemetry
User-facing stderr, HTTP JSON errors, stdio stdout, and exported telemetry must not contain `HEVY_API_KEY` values, `Authorization` / `Bearer` tokens, collector tokens, or raw probe error strings that embed secrets. Observer/user-hash paths must not stringify the API key. Debug dumps with `HEVY_MCP_DEBUG=1` stay on stderr and still redact keys.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: Sentinel keys absent from serialized logs, HTTP bodies, and span/Sentry payloads in existing node tests.

### VAL-NODE-028: Promise façade plus optional Effect variants stay compatible
After Effect adoption, `createNodeMcpServer`, `runStdioServer`, and `runServer` still return Promises usable from JS without Effect types. CLI `hevy-mcp` behavior above is unchanged. Any `*Effect` exports are additive. `arguments.ts` / `config.ts` remain throwing parsers (unknown option, invalid host/port/transport, `MissingHevyApiKeyError`) rather than Effect Config.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: `await createNodeMcpServer(...)` and `await runServer()` still work. `parseNodeCliOptions(["--unknown"])` throws `Unknown option: --unknown`. `assertApiKey("")` throws `MissingHevyApiKeyError`.

### VAL-NODE-029: Client disconnect mid-request evicts the HTTP session
After `POST /mcp` `tools/call` (or any in-flight session POST) has started, destroying the client connection before the response completes evicts that session. A later POST with the same `Mcp-Session-Id` returns 404 `{"error":"Unknown Mcp-Session-Id."}`. The session is not left reusable. The session lifecycle abort fires so in-flight handler work can stop.
Tool: vitest (real `node:http`)
Evidence: existing disconnect test in `packages/node/src/utils/streamable-http.test.ts`.

### VAL-NODE-030: Established-session GET/SSE is a first-class session route
`GET /mcp` with a valid `mcp-session-id` and `Accept: text/event-stream` returns HTTP 200 and keeps the stream open while the session lives. It does not allocate a second session id. `GET /mcp` without `Mcp-Session-Id` returns 400 with `{"error":"Mcp-Session-Id header is required."}` (same as non-initialize POST). Server/`handle.close()` ends the open stream.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: streamable-http GET/SSE tests.

### VAL-NODE-031: `runStdioServer` / `runServer` settle at start, not at shutdown
After a successful start (stdio connected or HTTP listening), the Promise returned by `runStdioServer()` / `runServer()` fulfills while the server is still running. It must not remain pending until SIGINT/SIGTERM. Shutdown still happens via signals / `target.close()` as in VAL-NODE-012. Help/version still fulfill without starting a transport (VAL-NODE-005/006).
Tool: vitest
Evidence: `packages/node/src/runtime.test.ts` / `node-lifecycle.test.ts`.

### VAL-NODE-032: Process exception tracking is lifecycle-scoped
Importing `hevy-mcp` does not add `uncaughtExceptionMonitor` / `unhandledRejection` listeners. Starting the executable lifecycle may add them. After graceful shutdown or the CLI fatal `process.exit(1)` path, those listeners are removed (or the process is exiting). A throw inside the exception tracker does not change MCP/HTTP outcomes and does not log secrets.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: listener-count / start-stop around lifecycle; no import-time Sentry/OTel (VAL-NODE-024).

### VAL-NODE-033: Update check never blocks lifecycle, stdout, or help
`--help` / `--version` / embedding import do not call `registry.npmjs.org` (or any update URL). After a successful server start, an update-check failure is swallowed (server stays up). If a notice is printed, it is stderr only, contains no API key / bearer / collector token, and does not appear on stdio MCP stdout. The check must not keep the process alive after shutdown.
Tool: vitest | node (spawned process)
Evidence: `packages/node/src/utils/version-check.test.ts`.

### VAL-NODE-034: Stdio `tools/call` stays JSON-RPC-on-stdout
Spawned `hevy-mcp` (fake/valid key, probe allowed to succeed or skip as in existing stdio lane) accepts JSON-RPC `tools/call` for a read tool and writes a JSON-RPC result frame on stdout. Log/shutdown/telemetry lines stay on stderr. A tools/call must not emit Effect/`Cause`/`Layer` strings on stdout. Do not require live Hevy.
Tool: node (`test:stdio` / pack smoke)
Evidence: stdio lane with the existing fake-key harness.

# Cross-Area Flows

## Surface

Composed user-facing path after Effect deepening: public Promise adapters collapse once at the adapter/tool/resource boundary into core tool runtime → operations `.effect()` → hevy-client request Effect → native `fetch`. Scope hierarchy is process (Node lifecycle/telemetry/signals) → server (MCP instance + exercise-template cache) → request (tool/resource, wired to `mcpReq.signal`) → hevy-client request Effect (retry/timeout; AbortSignal at the fetch edge only).

Deterministic validation uses fake credentials and mocked Hevy. Live Hevy is not required for this section.

## Interactions enumerated

- First visit: import `hevy-mcp` → `createNodeMcpServer` → MCP `tools/list` → `tools/call` of a read tool against mocked Hevy.
- Stdio/in-memory MCP tool call cancellation aborts Hevy fetch.
- Write tool never retried at the client.
- HTTP session close / process SIGTERM finalize telemetry and stop in-flight Hevy work.
- Server-scope cache does not outlive shutdown.
- CLI execute stays Promise-typed.
- Worker validation-cache does not inherit client 429-retry.
- Package boundaries, pack, changeset cascade.
- No secret leakage across layers; telemetry never changes outcomes.
- PR characterization baseline stays green.

## Assertions

### VAL-CROSS-001: First-visit embedding constructs a listable MCP server
Importing `hevy-mcp` and calling `createNodeMcpServer({ apiKey })` with a non-empty fake key returns a thenable that resolves to an MCP server. A connected MCP client can `tools/list` and observe the production Hevy tool catalog (read tools including `get-workouts`, write tools including `create-workout`). Construction does not read `process.env.HEVY_API_KEY`, does not probe Hevy, and does not start telemetry timers.
Tool: vitest (`packages/node/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/register.test.ts`, `pnpm run test:contract`)
Evidence: embedding entry is side-effect-free; register tests list tools over in-memory MCP.

### VAL-CROSS-002: First-visit read tool reaches mocked Hevy and returns structured content
After VAL-CROSS-001, `tools/call` of `get-workouts` (page/page_size) against a nocked `GET /v1/workouts` with a fake API key succeeds (`isError` falsy), includes `structuredContent.workouts`, and the text content parses to the same compact summaries. No live network. This is the navigable MCP surface, not a unit of `runToolEffect`.
Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:mcp` — `tests/integration/mocked/hevy-mcp.mocked.integration.test.ts`)
Evidence: mocked integration already drives Client ↔ McpServer ↔ Hevy nock for `get-workouts`.

### VAL-CROSS-003: In-memory and HTTP transports expose the same get-workouts contract
`get-workouts` with the capability-descriptor input yields the same structured output whether invoked over in-memory MCP, Node Streamable HTTP (`POST /mcp`), or the Worker HTTP harness used by the runtime contract matrix. Protocol version and output schema remain those of `getWorkoutsCapabilityDescriptor`. Spawned stdio `tools/call` is VAL-CROSS-024.
Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:contract` — `tests/contract/runtime-contract-matrix.test.ts`)
Evidence: contract matrix already posts the same tool across transports.

### VAL-CROSS-004: MCP request cancellation aborts the in-flight Hevy fetch
When an MCP client aborts a tool call (or `mcpReq.signal` is aborted) while Hevy `fetch` is outstanding, the native fetch is aborted (`AbortError` / `HEVY_REQUEST_ABORTED`), the tool returns a cancelled MCP error (`isError: true`, user message that the request was canceled, `errorOutcome.outcome === "cancelled"`), and no further Hevy attempt is dispatched after abort. Fiber interruption and fetch-edge AbortSignal may both fire; the observable requirement is that Hevy work stops.
Tool: vitest (core tool-runtime / mocked MCP; `pnpm run test:mcp` / `test:unit`)
Evidence: `define-tool.ts` already forwards `context.mcpReq.signal`; `runToolEffect` must keep that path live.

### VAL-CROSS-005: Process SIGTERM/SIGINT finalizes telemetry and closes the transport
On `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` after stdio or HTTP server start: the process lifecycle AbortSignal is aborted, `target.close()` runs, stdout flush is attempted, `flushTelemetry()` is awaited (bounded), and process exception listeners are removed. If close hangs, a forced-exit timer of 5_000 ms still terminates the process. No orphaned HTTP servers or stdio transports remain after the shutdown promise settles. Stopping in-flight Hevy work on that signal is VAL-CROSS-023; this assertion is transport/telemetry/forced-exit only.
Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:stdio`)
Evidence: graceful-shutdown / node-lifecycle tests.

### VAL-CROSS-006: HTTP session close stops in-flight Hevy work
Closing a Streamable HTTP session (client `DELETE`, dropped response, idle eviction, or server `close()`) aborts that session’s lifecycle signal, destroys open responses, closes the MCP transport and server, and causes any in-flight tool/resource Hevy fetch for that session to abort. Process-level `close()` aborts initializing controllers, closes every session, then closes the `node:http` listener; further `POST /mcp` receives 503 “shutting down”.
Tool: vitest (`packages/node/src/utils/streamable-http.test.ts`)
Evidence: `closeSession` aborts `lifecycleController` before transport/server close.

### VAL-CROSS-007: Server-scope cache does not outlive shutdown or cancelled owners
After MCP server `close()` or process lifecycle abort, an in-flight exercise-template catalog load (cache miss / `templates.listAll`) is interrupted and does not continue paging Hevy. A cancelled MCP request that is the only waiter for a cache-miss load does not leave that load running. If multiple waiters share a load, cancellation of one waiter must not silently ignore the canceller’s own request (it must stop for that request); document and test the shared-load policy explicitly (VAL-CORE-018 / VAL-CORE-019).
Tool: vitest (`packages/core/src/utils/exercise-template-catalog.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/resources/hevy.test.ts`)
Evidence: post-mission lookup must read request/server execution context.

The CLI does not import Node MCP runtime or Worker. A mocked `HevyClient` still serves list/get/create paths.
Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: `execute` signature is Promise; collapse helper is the only `runPromise`; `runCli` builds `createOperations(client)`.

### VAL-CROSS-009: Runtime-neutral packages stay free of Node and Cloudflare
`packages/hevy-client`, `packages/operations`, and `packages/core` contain no `node:` builtin imports, no `cloudflare:` imports, no `@cloudflare/` / `@sentry/` / `@opentelemetry/` runtime imports, and no imports of `hevy-mcp` or `@hevy-mcp/worker`. Dynamic non-literal `import()`/`require` remain forbidden in those packages.
Tool: pnpm (`pnpm run check:boundaries`); vitest (`tests/unit/package-boundaries.test.ts`)
Evidence: `repository/topology.json` `rejectBuiltins` / forbidden lists.

### VAL-CROSS-010: Adapters do not import one another
`packages/node` does not import `@hevy-mcp/worker` or `cloudflare:`. `packages/worker` does not import `hevy-mcp` / `@sentry/` / `@opentelemetry/` / `node:` builtins. `packages/cli` does not import Worker or Node runtime bootstrap. Allowed edges remain topology: node→core+hevy-client; worker→core+hevy-client; cli→core+hevy-client+operations.
Tool: pnpm (`pnpm run check:boundaries`)
Evidence: topology forbidden/allowed maps.

### VAL-CROSS-011: Public pack and types still load with additive Effect exports
After any Effect types appear in public `.d.ts` of `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `pnpm run test:pack` and `pnpm run test:pack:cli` still pack, install, and spawn the Node/CLI tarballs. `publint` in `test:pr` stays green. Existing Promise entry points remain callable without requiring callers to import `effect`.
Tool: pnpm (`pnpm run test:pack`, `pnpm run test:pack:cli`, `test:pr` publint member)
Evidence: adding `effect` as a runtime dep or bundling it is required if types leak.

### VAL-CROSS-012: Changeset cascade names every shipped consumer
A behavior or export change in `hevy-client` bumps `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. Operations → operations, core, hevy-mcp, worker, cli. Core → core, hevy-mcp, worker, cli. Node-only → `hevy-mcp` only. Worker-validation-cache-only → `@hevy-mcp/worker` only. Empty Changesets are illegal when any of those packages change. `pnpm run check:changeset` against `origin/main` passes.
Tool: pnpm (`pnpm run check:changeset`)
Evidence: `repository/topology.json` release bundles; AGENTS.md cascade table.

### VAL-CROSS-013: Write tools never retry at the Hevy client
A non-idempotent MCP write (`create-workout`, `create-routine`, `create-exercise-template`, `create-routine-folder`, `create-body-measurement`) that receives a transient Hevy failure (5xx, 429, network) produces exactly one HTTP attempt. The MCP error is terminal (`safe_to_retry` false / no second nock hit). Idempotent writes (`PUT` update-*) may retry only if current client policy for `idempotent-write` still allows it; POST/create must not. Operation `descriptor.safety === "non-idempotent-write"` is the authority once wired.
Tool: vitest (`packages/hevy-client` retry tests + MCP mocked write path / operations create descriptors)
Evidence: MCP/nock hit count = 1 for a mocked create-workout 503; plus client write-retry tests.

### VAL-CROSS-014: Worker validation-cache does not inherit client 429-retry
`validateHevyApiKeyResilient` on HTTP 429 throws after one validation attempt (no 300/600 ms backoff, no second `validate()` call). 503/408/network remain retryable up to 3 attempts with 300 then 600 ms delays, unless the signal is aborted or the deadline cannot cover the delay. Abort during delay fails (does not resolve-then-revalidate). The validation Hevy client is built with `maxGetRetries: 0`.
Tool: vitest (`packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`, `pnpm run test:worker`)
Evidence: `isRetryableValidationFailure` explicitly excludes 429; `createDefaultValidationClient` sets `maxGetRetries: 0`.

### VAL-CROSS-015: Client tagged errors remain discriminable through MCP and CLI
Throwing `ApiError` / `NetworkError` / `NotFoundError` / `RateLimitError` / `ValidationError` / `HevyHttpError` from the client Promise boundary still classifies as the same MCP `ErrorType` (`API_ERROR`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, `NOT_FOUND`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`) and the same CLI exit family (api vs network). Codes `HEVY_REQUEST_ABORTED`, `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` survive collapse. MCP `structuredContent.error` carries `outcome`, `phase`, `operation_safety`, `commit_state`, `safe_to_retry` without mutating the original error in place at the Promise boundary.
Tool: vitest (`packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.test.ts`, `error-handler.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/main.test.ts`)
Evidence: `determineErrorType` uses tagged classes; CLI `diagnostic()` branches on the same classes.

### VAL-CROSS-016: No secret leakage across layers
Logs, MCP error text, `SafeErrorDiagnostic`, CLI `--json` failures, Worker `console.warn`/`console.error` objects, and debug redaction never contain the `HEVY_API_KEY` value, `Authorization` / `api-key` header values, or raw Hevy error bodies beyond the bounded `responseError` sanitizer. Tool: vitest (`packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.test.ts`, `packages/hevy-client` response-error tests, `packages/node/src/utils/debug.test.ts`, CLI error tests)
Evidence: `createSafeErrorDiagnostic` omits messages/URLs; `sanitizeResponseErrorText` strips Bearer/api-key.

### VAL-CROSS-017: Telemetry failures never change tool or shutdown outcome
Observer `start`/`run`/`finish`, cache observers, MCP failure `console`/`Effect.log`, OTel/Sentry flush errors, and HTTP admission metrics must not fail a successful tool, convert a business error into a different MCP shape, or skip `target.close()`. Tool: vitest (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.test.ts`, `packages/node/src/utils/telemetry.test.ts`, `node-lifecycle.test.ts`)
Evidence: architecture requires telemetry sandboxing.

Covered by VAL-CROSS-001 (first-visit construction without probe/telemetry) and VAL-NODE-001 / VAL-NODE-024 (area owners). This id remains as the composed reminder that telemetry-as-Layer must not break embedding import, but validators should treat VAL-NODE-001 as the primary evidence. Tool: pnpm (`test:pr`, `check`, `check:types`, `build`, `test:performance`, `check:changeset`, `check:boundaries`)
Evidence: architecture §9 milestone gate; `docs/test-lanes.md` pull-request aggregate.

### VAL-CROSS-021: Read retries still honor Retry-After and never retry after caller abort
A read tool (`get-workouts`) that sees Hevy 429 with `Retry-After` delays at least that long (plus existing jitter bound) before a retry, and still stops immediately if the MCP/lifecycle signal aborts during backoff. Exhaustion surfaces `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` / MCP network error, not a hang. Worker validation-cache remains excluded from this policy (VAL-CROSS-014). MCP abort-during-backoff is also VAL-CROSS-004; this id owns the Retry-After ∩ abort conjunction.
Tool: vitest (`packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`, `backoff.test.ts`, `retry-schedule.test.ts`, plus an MCP interruption-during-backoff case)
Evidence: Retry-After delay bound plus abort-during-backoff with no extra fetch.

### VAL-CROSS-022: Promise façades remain the supported embedding/CLI surface
Callers using only Promises — `createHevyMcpServer`, `createNodeMcpServer`, `runStdioServer`, `runServer`, `HevyClient.getWorkouts` / `createWorkout`, operations `.execute()`, CLI `execute` — need no Effect knowledge. Any new `*Effect` exports are additive and do not replace those signatures. Generated Kubb functions and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` stay unpublished from `hevy-mcp` / CLI public exports.
Tool: vitest (`packages/node/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/hevy-client` public types, `packages/cli/src/commands/effect-collapse.test.ts`); pnpm (`test:pack`)
Evidence: architecture §7 public API stance.

Pass: the mocked fetch is aborted and does not complete after the signal; the process still follows VAL-CROSS-005 (close, bounded telemetry flush, no orphaned listener/server). Tool: vitest | node (`pnpm run test:stdio` / `test:mcp`)
Evidence: spawned stdio JSON-RPC frames for `get-workouts`.

A failing Hevy call (401, 5xx, abort, deadline) through (a) MCP `tools/call`, (b) CLI `execute` / `--json`, and (c) Node HTTP error JSON / stderr must not contain `Cause`, `Fiber`, `Layer`, `ManagedRuntime`, or raw Effect `toString` dumps. User-facing strings stay the existing MCP/CLI families (VAL-CROSS-015). Secrets remain covered by VAL-CROSS-016.

# Review: Live E2E, CLI, Docs (VAL-LIVE-*, VAL-CLI-*, VAL-DOCS-*)

Scope: black-box gaps vs mission.md Milestone 4 + architecture.md §9 live lanes. Do not require Worker-wide Effect, live Worker HTTP, or secret leakage.

## Verdict

The live/CLI/docs area is mostly well bounded. VAL-LIVE-006 correctly keeps `test:worker-http:live` / `HEVY_RUN_LIVE_WORKER_TESTS` **out** of milestone 4. Secret handling is stated (VAL-LIVE-007, VAL-CLI-002, VAL-DOCS-004, plus contract header). Remaining issues are a few real coverage holes and two over-tight live assertions that can fail on empty accounts.

## Over-scoping (do not add / keep excluded)

- Do **not** require `pnpm run test:worker-http:live` or `HEVY_RUN_LIVE_WORKER_TESTS=1`. Architecture: Worker beyond validation-cache is out of scope; VAL-LIVE-006 is correct.
- Do **not** require a live CLI canary (`hevy workouts list` against real Hevy). VAL-CLI-003 is correct; CLI is Promise-adapter characterization via `test:cli`.
- Do **not** require live MCP writes, catalog pagination against production, or live cancellation/timeout against Hevy (those belong in mocked/unit lanes).
- Do **not** require `pnpm run inspect` or browser MCP clients (CONTRIBUTING known-fragile).
- Do **not** assert Effect internals (`ManagedRuntime`, `Effect.retry`) in README as implementation names; VAL-DOCS-001 already stays at control-structure / scope hierarchy, which is appropriate.

## Secret handling (keep / slightly tighten wording)

Existing:

- Contract header: never print/log/persist `HEVY_API_KEY`, `Authorization` / `api-key`, bearer tokens.
- VAL-LIVE-001/007: captured output and `test-results/release-source.json` must not contain the key.
- VAL-CLI-002: stderr may contain the **variable name** only.
- VAL-DOCS-004 / VAL-CLI-004: keys in `.env` or process env, never argv/URLs/logs/fixtures; docs use placeholders.

Keep these. Validators must redact keys in reports even when inspecting artifacts.

Gap (small): VAL-LIVE-001 does not say how validators **obtain** the key (worktree `.env` only, never `echo $HEVY_API_KEY` / `printenv`). Propose VAL-LIVE-009.

## Real gaps — proposed assertions

### VAL-LIVE-009: Validators never dump the live key to obtain it

Before `test:live`, presence of `HEVY_API_KEY` is checked without printing the value (`test -n "${HEVY_API_KEY-}"` or a redacted preflight). Commands never pass the key as a CLI argument or URL query. Reports quote only redacted output.

Tool: process env / Read of command logs  
Evidence: no key substring in validator transcripts.

### VAL-LIVE-010: Full PR baseline still runs in milestone 4 (without live key for PR lanes)

Mission Milestone 4 is “full PR baseline **plus** live lanes.” VAL-LIVE-008 covers `test:pr` / `test:cli` not needing a live key, but does not require the architecture §9 gate itself in this area. Add: with `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false`, `check`, `check:types`, `build`, `test:pr`, `test:performance`, `check:changeset`, `check:boundaries` still exit 0 on the feature branch **without** a live key. Live lanes are additional, not a substitute.

Tool: pnpm  
Evidence: exit codes; no `api.hevyapp.com` from those commands.

(If CROSS already owns this as VAL-CROSS-020, do not duplicate as a hard extra gate—cross-reference only. Prefer a one-line “see VAL-CROSS-020; live does not replace it” note under VAL-LIVE-008 rather than a new ID if CROSS is the owner.)

### VAL-LIVE-003 loosen: empty lists must not fail the canary

VAL-LIVE-003 currently requires workouts to be a **non-empty** array with first-item `id`/`title` length ≥ 3. A valid key on an empty Hevy account would fail the mission despite a successful API. Architecture/mission only require live lanes against the real API, not populated data.

**Change VAL-LIVE-003** (not a new ID): workouts/routines/body-measurements responses parse as arrays; **if non-empty**, first items expose the documented fields. Empty arrays are a pass. Do not create resources to populate data.

### VAL-DOCS-005: CONTRIBUTING / architecture docs name live commands and MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false

VAL-DOCS-001 covers README + `docs/architecture.md` control structure. VAL-DOCS-004 covers credential vs PR split. Missing: operator docs still tell workers to prefix `mise exec` with `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false` (mission environment constraint) and that live runs only in milestone 4 from the worktree `.env`.

Proposed assertion: `CONTRIBUTING.md` and/or `docs/test-lanes.md` still document `test:live` / `test:integration` as credential-gated; they do not instruct unscoped `mise exec --` without `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false` as the required recipe for this environment. They do not add Worker live canaries to the PR/milestone-4 gate.

Tool: Read  
Evidence: file contents.

### VAL-CLI-005: CLI JSON / exit families stay secret-free on mocked failures (optional if CROSS covers)

VAL-CLI-001/002 cover happy mocked adapter and missing-key. If not already VAL-CROSS-015/016: a mocked 401/network failure through `execute` still exits in the documented 0–4 family, `--json` error objects omit the API key and raw Authorization, and Effect/`Cause` strings are absent.

Only add if CROSS does not already bind CLI error JSON. Prefer not to duplicate VAL-CROSS-016.

## Non-gaps (already covered — do not add)

- Missing-key fail-closed for `test:live` (VAL-LIVE-002).
- `test:integration` skip-without-key vs fail-closed live traffic (VAL-LIVE-005).
- Read-only live tools list (VAL-LIVE-003 intent).
- No live Worker HTTP (VAL-LIVE-006).
- CLI not in live file (VAL-CLI-003).
- Docs anti-claims for Worker-wide Effect, Zod Schema, Effect Config, Kubb public API (VAL-DOCS-002).
- Node README embedding contract (VAL-DOCS-003).

## Summary of recommended contract edits

1. Loosen VAL-LIVE-003 empty-account workouts.
2. Add VAL-LIVE-009 (never dump key).
3. Cross-link VAL-LIVE-008 → VAL-CROSS-020 instead of a second full gate, unless live area is the only milestone-4 owner.
4. Add VAL-DOCS-005 (live lane docs + MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false; still no worker-http:live).
5. Do not add live CLI, live Worker HTTP, or live writes.

# Review: Cross-Area Flows (VAL-CROSS-*)

Review of `validation-contract.md` Cross-Area Flows against `architecture.md` and `mission.md`. Area assertions were skimmed only to detect composed flows that no area owns, and to separate fine overlaps from true duplicates.

Focus: first-visit, cancellation across layers, shutdown stopping Hevy work, write no-retry, worker 429 divergence, boundaries, pack, changeset, PR baseline, secret leakage, Promise façades.

---

## Verdict

The CROSS section already names the right composed path (Promise adapter → core runtime → operations `.effect()` → hevy-client request Effect → native `fetch`) and the process → server → request → fetch-edge AbortSignal hierarchy. Most VAL-CROSS-* items are **legitimate composed views** of area assertions, not redundant unit tests.

Two real composed-flow gaps remain:

1. **Process shutdown must stop in-flight Hevy work** (stdio/HTTP SIGTERM/SIGINT → lifecycle → server Scope → request fiber → native `fetch`). VAL-CROSS-005 closes the transport and flushes telemetry; it never says the hanging Hevy call aborts. VAL-CORE-024 and VAL-NODE-012 each cover one layer only.
2. **Stdio is missing from the multi-transport first-visit/read contract.** VAL-CROSS-003 lists in-memory MCP, Node Streamable HTTP, and the Worker HTTP harness — not spawned stdio `tools/call`. VAL-NODE-011 is `initialize` + `tools/list` only.

One Promise-collapse gap is worth a CROSS id because no single area owns all three collapse surfaces:

3. **Cause / Effect internals must not leak through MCP, CLI, or Node stderr** after collapse. Core covers MCP (`VAL-CORE-002` / `010` / `012`); CLI and Node do not assert the same “no `Cause` / `Layer` / fiber dump” rule.

Everything else in the focus list is already asserted, either as a CROSS flow or as an area assertion whose composition is implied. Do not mint CROSS ids that only restated VAL-CLIENT / VAL-CORE / VAL-NODE / VAL-WORKER.

---

## Proposed new assertions

### VAL-CROSS-023: Process shutdown aborts in-flight Hevy work

**Why it is composed (not an area restatement).** Architecture §2–§3: process Scope owns SIGINT/SIGTERM and `lifecycleSignal`; that signal interrupts the server Scope; request fibers must stop; AbortSignal is bridged at the fetch edge only. VAL-CROSS-005 asserts transport close + telemetry flush + 5s forced-exit. VAL-NODE-012 asserts “active work tied to the lifecycle abort signal is cancelled” without mentioning Hevy `fetch`. VAL-CORE-024 asserts `lifecycleSignal` abort in core isolation. VAL-CROSS-006 covers **HTTP session** close, not process SIGTERM on stdio. VAL-CROSS-007 covers **catalog** paging after server close, not a hanging `get-workouts` fetch.

**Black-box assertion.** After stdio or HTTP `hevy-mcp` is running with a fake key, start a `tools/call` (or catalog miss) against a hanging mocked Hevy GET. Deliver SIGINT or SIGTERM. Pass: the mocked fetch is aborted (`AbortError` / caller signal aborted) and does not complete after the signal; the process still follows VAL-CROSS-005 (close, bounded telemetry flush, no orphaned listener/server). Fail: Hevy retries or body read continue after shutdown, or shutdown waits on Hevy retry/backoff.

Scope hierarchy is process (Node lifecycle/telemetry/signals) → server (MCP instance + exercise-template cache) → request (tool/resource, wired to `mcpReq.signal`) → hevy-client request Effect (retry/timeout; AbortSignal at the fetch edge only).

Public Promise APIs remain (`createNodeMcpServer`, `runStdioServer`/`runServer`, `HevyClient` methods, operations `.execute()`, CLI `execute`). Effect types may appear in public exports as additive. Worker request handling, OAuth, Zod→Schema, Effect Config, and generated Kubb output are out of scope.

## Interactions enumerated

- First visit: import `hevy-mcp` → `createNodeMcpServer({ apiKey })` (or `createHevyMcpServer`) → MCP `tools/list` → `tools/call` of a read tool against a mocked Hevy API.

- Write tool (`create-workout` and other `kind: "write"` / `non-idempotent-write` operations): one Hevy attempt; client retry schedule must not re-dispatch.
- HTTP session: `DELETE` session, client disconnect, idle eviction, or process `close()` aborts the session lifecycle signal, closes transports/servers, and stops in-flight Hevy work for that session.
- Process `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`: abort process lifecycle signal, `target.close()` (stdio server or HTTP session graph), flush telemetry, then forced-exit deadline (~5s) if close hangs.
- Server close / process shutdown interrupts the server-owned exercise-template cache; a cancelled cache-miss load must not continue paging Hevy after the owning request or server is gone.
- CLI `execute` remains `Promise`-typed, constructs operations from the curated client, and collapses Effect once via `Effect.runPromise`.
- Worker validation-cache: own Schedule (delays 300/600ms, max 3 attempts); HTTP 429 is not retried; validation client is constructed with `maxGetRetries: 0`. Must not inherit hevy-client’s 429-as-transient policy.
- Package boundaries: `hevy-client` / `operations` / `core` have no `node:` or `cloudflare:` imports; Node does not import Worker; adapters do not import one another.
- Error classes (`ApiError`, `NetworkError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError`, `ValidationError`, `HevyHttpError` plus `HEVY_*` codes) survive the Promise/MCP/CLI collapse with the same discriminators; MCP error policy emits bounded `SafeErrorDiagnostic` / `createErrorResponse` shapes, never raw keys.
